newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Extra Telstra money to pay debt - Costello.
newsitem.headline: Extra Telstra money to pay debt - Costello.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that the government would use any extra money from the part sale of government-owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp to repay debt.
"It'll be used to retire debt," Costello said when asked what the government would do if the partial sale raised more than the expected A$8 billion.
"Any additional asset sales from now on retires debt," Costello told the National Press Club in the annual post-budget appearance.

Costello on Tuesday unveiled the government's budget for the fiscal year from July, projecting an underlying budget -- before windfalls such as asset sales -- of A$3.85 billion, down from A$6.86 billion a year earlier.
The budget also allocated A$5 billion to repay debt.
The budget papers show the government expects to raise about A$9.83 billion, largely from selling one third of Telstra and selling long-term leases for three capital city airports.
Analysts have long considered the government's estimation of A$8 billion from the Telstra privatisation to be conservative.
